title: Optimistic client-wallet with server reconciliation for metered ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: At-least-once ingestion and client retries cause duplicate metering events and occasional double-charges. Existing server-side fence techniques add latency or require global coordination that hurts tail latency. Goal: prototype and ship an 'optimistic client-wallet' pattern where SDKs make a lightweight local reservation and the server accepts short-lived reservations with a reconciliation sweep to guarantee eventual correctness.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes reserve/commit/abort primitives and falls back to synchronous commit when necessary
Server accepts reservation requests and exposes a reconciliation API to reconcile permanent commits against outstanding reservations
E2E tests show >=99.995% avoidance of duplicate billed units for typical retry scenarios (3 retries) without added client roundtrips in the common path
Reconciliation sweep resolves mismatches within configured window (default 24h) and generates flags for manual review when >0.1% drift is found
Metrics and dashboards show reservation hit/miss rate, stale-reservation count, reconciliation corrections, and cost impact estimates
Security review completed for reservation token format and KMS usage
implementation_notes: Design summary: 1) Client SDK maintains a local monotonic local-wallet counter per API key and attempts an optimistic 'reserve' RPC which allocates a small ephemeral reservation record (reservation_id, reserved_units, ttl, client_sequence). The reserve RPC is best-effort: if the server is unreachable or rejects, SDK falls back to a normal commit. 2) Commit RPC is idempotent and references the reservation_id when present; server marks reservation fulfilled and materializes ledger entries. 3) Reconciliation service periodically scans reservations older than ttl and compares committed ledger vs reservation ledger. Drift is corrected via reconciliation transactions and incident logs. 4) Data model: per-customer reservation table keyed by (customer_id, reservation_id) with state {reserved_units, client_sequence, created_at, ttl, committed} and a per-customer ledger for permanent commits. 5) TTL/Garbage collection: reservations auto-expire after configurable TTL (default 30s) and GC after 7d. 6) SDK fallbacks: if reservation not acknowledged, SDK will retry commit but include deterministic commit_id (canonicalized request hash + client_wallet_counter) so server deduplicates. 7) Operational controls: reconciliation threshold configuration, emergency purge, and conservative default reservation sizes to bound temporary credit exposure.
progress_updates: 2026-01-12: Spike complete. Benchmarked reserve+commit flow against a synthetic dialog workload; median latency improvement ~6ms vs synchronous commit for happy path.
2026-01-18: Prototype SDK for Node and Python with local-wallet counter implemented. Added deterministic commit_id generation using SHA256(canonicalized_payload + client_seq).
2026-01-25: Backend reservation table schema PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/prs/2357. Initial integration tests passing on staging.

2026-02-02: QA found an edge case where client restarts can reuse local counter leading to conflicting reservation_ids; mitigated by adding ephemeral random suffix to client_sequence and persisting wallet state to disk in SDK.
2026-02-10: Load test (10k rps) shows reservation table write amplification acceptable; increased GC window to 7 days for safe reconciliation.
2026-02-15: Integration with billing pipeline done, reconciliation agent in alpha. Filing follow-up for disaster-recovery playbook.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan): Appreciate latency gains; ask: what is the customer-visible failure mode when reconciliation fails? Ensure clear billing credits path.
Security (Maya): Reservation token is effectively a debit authorization; require KMS-signed reservation IDs or short-lived HMAC using per-customer key. Also request a threat model doc.
Reliability (Omar): Concern about multi-region races where two regions accept reservations for same customer. Suggest single-writer reconciliation leader per-customer and region-aware routing.
Design (Priya): Recommend a UX story for customers to opt-out of optimistic reservations for high-assurance billing accounts.
